question.text: A 'side pocket' provision in an AIF's fund documents is BEST described as:

answer.text: A fee-sharing arrangement between placement agents
A mechanism to segregate illiquid or distressed investments into a separate accounting compartment, so valuation / redemption issues do not contaminate the main portfolio
A type of co-investment opportunity offered to anchor LPs
A regulatory reserve required under SEBI (AIF) Regulations at 5% of corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: A side pocket segregates illiquid/distressed or hard-to-value positions into a separate accounting bucket; main portfolio NAV is shielded, and LP redemptions/distributions are processed against the clean portfolio while the side-pocketed position is realised over time. The Trap: Option A is an unrelated revenue-share. Option C is co-investment. Option D fabricates a regulatory reserve. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests side-pocketing mechanics for Cat III open-ended in particular; XIX-A/B do not. Manager's Pro-Tip: Disclose side-pocket activation criteria objectively in the PPM (e.g., 'any position unable to be marked for 30 consecutive days using observable inputs') — discretionary side-pockets invite LP disputes and SEBI scrutiny.
